auditNotes: Audited main at the PR #12 merge. Its 25 November 2026 post-merge CI proof includes all 13 stages, five PostgreSQL migration tests, 22 tenant-isolation regressions, 26 mail cases, 14 authorization cases, three import cases, API smoke and three browser cases.

Reviewed 41 frontend page files, 24 components, 32 route files, 9 middleware files, 34 services, 8 standalone migrations, 9 server test/support files, 12 scripts and the existing integration workflow. The 423 static router declarations include compatibility and unmounted endpoints. The 122 literal table declarations describe source schema, not database contents.

Reviewed closed PRs #1–#3, merged PRs #4 and #9–#12, and open PRs #5, #7 and #8. PRs #5 and #7 offer overlapping branch-only SSKEMS intake options. PR #8 records historical A01 findings, with CI, parent lookup and PostgreSQL changes superseded by later merges.

The existing Institute OS checkout was clean at audit start. The primary experiment worktree had 4 status entries, the security prototype had 70, and A01 and A02 were clean. These linked worktrees share one stash. The separate Desktop CRM clone had 59 status entries and zero stashes. Local and stash metadata were inspected without reading private changes. The local A01 branch contains one extra documentation commit beyond PR #8.

Cross-checked all tracked page, route and service paths against the inventory. Six empty route placeholders and four dormant utility modules were classified as supporting source. Active mount evidence is linked under its logical feature.

The owner-approved scope follows the Phase A security foundation before the Phase B workflow. Repository-observed features and proposed roadmap capabilities are classified separately. Branch candidates do not establish behaviour on main.

Feature evidence is from tracked source and scoped synthetic test results. External delivery, two-tenant staging, operational backup scheduling and restore acceptance remain open. The audit did not access credentials, production records or staging databases.
